name: LLM-Integrated Exam System
tagline: Team-built exam and learning platform with LLM-assisted grading and event-driven microservices
description:
Backend architecture, database schema, microservices, and Kubernetes deployment for a university digital exam platform. Features high-concurrency assessment delivery, automated evaluation pipelines, and integrated Azure OpenAI assistance for preliminary free-text grading.

Christian co-led the backend of the exam platform and contributed to green LMS as part of its eight-person student team.

green LMS is the result of the RWTH Aachen University practical lab “Advanced Web Technologies: Integration of AI approaches into an LMS” (SS25), run by the Learning Technologies Research Group (Informatik 9) and supervised by Dr. Volodymyr Sokol. An eight-person student team was asked to rebuild the checkpoint and assessment workflow of the university's existing learning management system as a set of independently deployable microservices.

The system is split into a thin Express gateway and six domain services. The gateway terminates HTTP, handles sessions and permissions, validates payloads with Joi, and routes requests to the checkpoint, challenge, progress, assessment, file and statistics services. Services communicate asynchronously over NATS for events such as checkpoint publication and grading updates, cache hot state in Redis, and persist everything in a shared PostgreSQL schema modelled around subjects, branches, checkpoints, question slots, questions and marks.

The front end is a React 18 single-page application with role-aware routing for students and teachers, a checkpoint editor that assembles sections from question pools, drag-and-drop and multiple-choice question types, and a live progress view while a checkpoint is being worked on. Every repository had a GitLab CI pipeline that built the service image and deployed it to the course Kubernetes cluster on merges to main.
purpose: To add free-text questions and preliminary grading to an existing examination system for a Ukrainian university, and to rebuild the checkpoint and assessment workflow of the RWTH Aachen learning management system as independently deployable microservices.
strengths: Deployed the application stack with Kubernetes
Designed SQL schemas for exam submissions
Built the Azure OpenAI pre-evaluation of open-text answers, comparing against teacher reference answers with temperature-0 grading (~$0.0033 and 4-7 s per answer on gpt-4o-mini)
Split the LMS into seven independently deployable Node.js services behind a single Express gateway
Modelled checkpoints, question slots, answer types and fractional marks in a PostgreSQL schema shared across services
Used NATS pub/sub for asynchronous service events and Redis for cached state instead of synchronous request chains
Built a React 18 teacher and student interface with a Vite proxy layer, Redux state and role-aware routing
Deployed every merge on main through a shared GitLab CI template into the course Kubernetes cluster
limitations: The course infrastructure (Kubernetes cluster, managed PostgreSQL, NATS deployment) was decommissioned after the lab, so no live demo is available
The source repositories are private course artefacts; the GitHub mirrors are kept for archival, statistics and code exploration
The shared utility package is published to a university-internal npm registry, which makes reproduction outside the course network non-trivial
installation:
# Node.js 16 and access to the private mirrors are required
for s in gateway gateway-files challenges checkpoints progress shared-utils ui-2.0; do
  git clone git@github.com:chrisb09/green-lms-$s.git
done

# each service reads its configuration from environment variables
# (PostgreSQL, NATS, Redis); the shipped set-env-dev.sh is redacted
cd green-lms-gateway
set -a && . ./set-env-dev.sh && set +a
npm install
usage:
# start a service, e.g. the gateway on :3030
npm start

# start the file service on :3031 and the UI on :3000 against them
npm start --prefix ../green-lms-gateway-files
cd ../green-lms-ui-2.0
npm run start
